subject: Pctl cutover & fallback criteria for hosted P50/P95 commitments
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosted API P50/P95 proposal + measurement definition (initial)

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As promised, attaching a concise proposal for the latency commitments Pioneer asked for while we finalize commercial terms. High level:

- Candidate commitments (hosted): p50 = 35ms, p95 = 225ms (edge region: us-west)
- Measurement epoch: 24-hour rolling window, aggregated daily, with availability of per-route / per-model telemetry for audits
- Cutover / fallback criteria: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (lower-cost/quantized) when sustained p95 degradation exceeds 10% for >30 minutes; manual escalation if degradation persists >3 hours

Attachment: redwood-measurement-definition.pdf (definitions + sample telemetry)

Two asks from your side to proceed:
1) Confirm whether the 24-hour rolling aggregation is acceptable vs. a calendar-day bucket.
2) Confirm whether Pioneer wants regional carveouts for scheduled maintenance windows.

If that looks good, Vanessa and I will prep a short addendum.

Thanks,
Soojin

Soojin —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the PDF. A few clarifying questions from our SRE/procurement team:

1) Why a 24-hour rolling window instead of fixed UTC-day buckets? Our billing/operational reporting uses calendar days for SLAs.
2) The fallback language (>=10% p95 degradation >30m) — can you be more specific about how you compute the baseline (moving baseline or fixed from go-live)?
3) If Redwood triggers automatic fallback to a quantized variant, will Pioneer see an explicit signal in the response headers or a separate webhook? We need auditable evidence for our incident postmortems.

Also attaching a short spreadsheet (pioneer-slo-request.xlsx) with our preferred cutover thresholds and a column for legal redlines.

Thanks — Amit

Subject: Fwd: Pioneer questions on measurement / fallback — need input

Karthik/Marissa —

Forwarding Amit's questions. Quick notes from my side:
- Rolling 24h vs calendar day: rolling smooths transient spikes during daylight bursts; calendar day aligns to customer's ops. Pioneer prefers calendar days.
- Baseline computation: we currently use a 7-day moving baseline for regression detection; the product team can also pin a fixed baseline at go-live for contract purposes.
- Signal: runtime emits a header X-Redwood-Fallback: variant=quantized; timestamp=... and we can surface a webhook to Pioneer’s incident system.

What language should we propose in the addendum to balance operability and legal clarity? Also, possible acceptance criteria for fallback (automated vs manual) that won't trigger a breach?

Soojin

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pioneer questions on measurement / fallback — need input

Soojin — quick draft guidance below (high level):

1) Measurement window: offer both options — default to 24-hour rolling for hosted telemetry (operationally more stable), with contract option to switch to calendar-day buckets for billing. Add a 30-day notice for switching measurement mode to avoid immediate churn.

2) Baseline: propose a dual-mode baseline — default 7-day moving baseline for automated detection + option to fix baseline at go-live for the first 90 days post-cutover (after which moving baseline applies), unless both parties agree to an extension. This prevents transient cutovers being considered long-term degradations.

3) Fallback & evidence: commit to emitting X-Redwood-Fallback header *and* a webhook to Pioneer with timestamp, fallback_reason, and fallback_variant. Preserve webhook events for 90 days in audit logs (longer retention available as add-on). Automated fallback should not, by itself, constitute breach if variant is compatible and Pioneer chooses to continue traffic — consider a grace window of 3 hours post-first-fallback event before a breach countable incident.

4) Escalation: if degradation persists beyond 3 hours or if fallback is ineffective and customer impact observed, automatic escalation to SOC/CS/solutions on-call.

That should balance product flexibility + contract clarity. Happy to write up more formal addendum language.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API P50/P95 proposal + measurement definition (proposal update)

Hi Amit —

Thanks for the spreadsheet — see inline answers below and a concise proposal we think meets Pioneer’s audit and procurement needs:

- Measurement window: default = 24-hour rolling (operational). For contract/billing, we will use calendar-day buckets if Pioneer selects that option in the addendum; switching measurement mode requires 30-day notice.

- Baseline: apply a 7-day moving baseline for automated detection. Option (one-time at go-live) to pin a fixed baseline for the first 90 days post-cutover; thereafter moving baseline resumes unless both parties agree otherwise.

- Fallback evidence: runtime will include an X-Redwood-Fallback header on responses and push a webhook to Pioneer’s incident URL containing: timestamp, fallback_variant, fallback_reason, and a reference to the request_id batch. We will retain those webhook events/audit logs for 90 days by default.

- Fallback & breach threshold: automated fallback is allowed and will not count as SLA breach if the fallback successfully restores responses and Pioneer elects to continue using the variant. We propose a 3-hour grace window after the first automated fallback event; if p95 remains outside the committed threshold for >3 hours despite fallbacks, that will be evaluated as a potential SLA incident and subject to normal remediation/credit calculations.

Next steps: Vanessa will prepare an addendum draft with these items called out (measurement mode, baseline rules, fallback signal & retention, 3-hour grace, escalation path). If procurement/legal want alternative phrasing we can iterate quickly.

Best,
Soojin
